findings.detail: walk_support_connected joins reversed and forward prefixes of the actual original walk, keeping every support vertex inside that walk. triangleModel_of_internal_walk uses the two distinct adjacent endpoint singletons and the internal walk support as three actual nonempty branches. The supplied endpoint exclusions establish disjointness; internal support connectivity is proved; and all six oriented clique adjacencies are witnessed by host edges. triangle_minor_of_alternative_path excludes the zero/one-edge degeneracies and uses path support nodup plus dropLast to remove the second endpoint while retaining its penultimate incident edge. triangle_minor_of_cycle obtains this alternative path from an actual cycle. Therefore K3-minor exclusion implies actual acyclicity, with no graph-size, finite-host, forest-oracle or contraction-label assumption.

A genuine input MST supplies an actual spanning tree on the whole vertex type. tree_eq_forest uses its connectedness and the maximal-acyclic characterization to show a spanning tree inside an acyclic host equals that host. For h=3 the previous cycle result therefore forces G=T. The output reuses this same finite graph with unit weights and proves genuine minimum-spanning-tree minimality by equality of every spanning-tree weight. Positive edge weights and n>=2 establish strictly positive original and unit MST totals before simplifying both lightness ratios to 1, so the required factor-1/2 bound is meaningful. Weighted girth follows vacuously from absence of cycles, and n<=2n-1 is explicit. The combined theorem splits h>=3 into h=3 or h>=4 and invokes the previously proved actual repeated subdivision/scaling/rounding theorem in the latter case. The output contains a literal finite graph, literal MST, edge weights >=1, unit tree weights, retained weighted girth, genuine K_h-minor exclusion, at most 2n-1 vertices and at least half the original lightness. No hidden nonforest premise appears.

IsBounded bounds the cardinality of each actual branch set by a natural number. Composition uses exactly the union of host branches over each intermediate branch from the proved genuine minor composition. The finset biUnion count gives at most m*n vertices; disjointness and connectedness remain those of the actual composition theorem. induceTarget restricts target vertices while retaining their exact old branch sets and all induced-target edges. exists_host_subgraph takes the actual union of all branches, bounds its size by m times the target cardinality, restricts the full minor to the actual induced host graph and invokes the genuine edge-count inequality. That inequality assigns each branch a unique label and injects distinct target edges into host-edge images, so the preserved edge count is not a quotient-label surrogate. Empty target or width zero does not create a missing positivity condition.

The natural ceiling is used only with nonnegative epsilon*d. For K>=1, d>=2 and 0<=epsilon<=1, ceil(epsilon*d)<epsilon*d+1 gives the stated 1+Kd+ceil(epsilon*d)<=3Kd. For K,d>=1 the analogous 4Kd bound is valid. The rational instance K=1,d=11/10,epsilon=99/100 has ceil(epsilon*d)=2, so the displayed 3Kd arithmetic fails as 41/10>33/10. This theorem refutes only the printed intermediate arithmetic inequality. It is neither a graph counterexample to Proposition 3.2 nor a counterexample to any main theorem; the actual next module recovers the original 3Kd graph conclusion on the full printed domain.

The selected mates are a Finset subset of actual vertices, with cardinality exactly ceil(epsilon1*d); their distinctness is intrinsic, not merely a list-length assertion. The induced vertex set is N(v) union M. Every common neighbor of v and a selected mate w belongs to N(v), and its edge to w survives this induction. The map from each common-neighbor subtype to the induced neighbor subtype is injective. The selected-vertex map M to S is injective, so summing these lower bounds counts only distinct degree terms and is bounded by the full degree sum 2|E(G[S])|. Thus possible common-neighbor overlaps or mate-to-mate edges are safely accounted for with the factor 1/2. Nat.ceil_le converts the real mate-count assumption into the exact selectable natural cardinality, and Nat.le_ceil supplies the reverse inequality used for the edge lower bound. Nonnegative epsilon2*d justifies multiplication. The omitted extra v saves one vertex; |S|<=Kd+ceil(epsilon1*d)<Kd+d+1<=3Kd under K,d>=1. The resulting alternative uses a literal induced finite simple graph and proves the original vertex and edge constants.

The small-dense alternative is first obtained in the actual target F. Restricting the actual minor model to its selected target set yields an induced-target model with unchanged natural branch bound m. The proved host-subgraph extraction then returns an actual induced subgraph G[T] with |T|<=m|S| and at least all edges of F[S]. Fintype.card of the selected subtype is explicitly identified with S.card before converting counts to real values. Since natural m>=0, multiplication gives the claimed 3mKd vertex bound and preserves epsilon1*epsilon2*d^2/2 edges. The alternative Unmated predicate is on F, as required for Corollary 3.3. This is the natural-width interface only; it does not state arbitrary-real-width Corollary 3.3.

For natural k>=100, the ceiling lower bound and ceil(k/6)<k/6+1 give k/6<=ell<=k/5. With d>=k^2, d is nonnegative, k>0 and 6/k<=1/2, so d0=(1-6/k)d>=d/2. Nonnegativity of ell and k/5 justifies squaring ell<=k/5; ell^2<=k^2/25<=d/2<=d0 proves the exact Theorem 3.6 density parameter requirement when epsilon2,0=1/ell^2. The proof never claims the false d0>=k^2. The coefficient identity (1/k)(1/k)d^2/2=d^2/(2k^2) is exact; Lean field division even makes its unconstrained k=0 case valid. These are arithmetic lemmas only and contain no hidden graph-existence premise or purported proof of technical Theorems 3.6 or 3.7.

domain_and_correspondence_notes: The source graphs are finite and simple, matching Fintype and SimpleGraph. No multigraph degree or average-degree convention is silently used.

Proposition 3.2 is proved for real K,d>=1, epsilon1 in [0,1] and epsilon2>=0. This contains its printed epsilon1,epsilon2 in (0,1) domain and handles weak zero boundaries directly, including an empty selected set when epsilon1=0. No epsilon2<=1 assumption is needed.

The mate filter counts actual host vertices satisfying the common-neighbor threshold, with no explicit w!=v condition. Definition 3.1 likewise imposes no explicit distinct-from-v clause. The selected mates themselves are pairwise distinct. Even if v is selected, the induced-incidence proof remains correct; a convention excluding v would only weaken the Unmated conclusion and does not invalidate the printed alternative.

Corollary 3.3 is certified for natural branch-cardinality bound m, exactly the interface claimed by this package and required by the later integer-width construction. No arbitrary-real-width theorem is advertised.

The normalization theorem is explicitly for h>=3, n>=2, nonnegative girth threshold and positive graph-edge weights, with a genuine input MST. The h=3 subtheorem even works for arbitrary real girth threshold because the host is acyclic. Empty/singleton lightness and h=1,2 are outside the combined theorem.

The source density is e(G)/v(G), not average degree. The reviewed graph alternatives state edge and vertex counts rather than dividing by possibly zero order. With the printed positive epsilon parameters their positive edge bound makes any dense witness nonempty; zero-boundary extensions need no positive-density claim.
